claim: GRAMMAR 3, (わたしは) body part が いたいです, is shown by many cards but explained on none: no back says the painful part takes が or that the subject is always the speaker.
evidence: Book GRAMMAR 3: 'This expression is used when stating that some part of the body hurts. The painful part of the body takes the particle が. The subject of the sentence is always the speaker, and わたしは is usually omitted.' Cards atama-ga-itaidesu, itai-hurts, kata-ga-itai, nodo-ga-itai, symptom-tooth-hurts, senaka-ga-itai, koshi-ga-itai carry no note.
fix: Add a note to chapter-21/atama-ga-itaidesu (or itai-hurts) stating that the body part takes が and that the speaker is the unstated subject.

claim: Exercise II item 4 asks for あした やすんでも いいですか, and neither that sentence nor the て-form やすんで is on any card in the deck.
evidence: Book Exercise II: '4. あした やすみます。 →' (pattern: ～ても いいですか), with やすみます glossed 'take a day off'. The extras card the other five items each have (ask-open-window, kaaten-shimete-mo-ii, denki-tsukete-mo-ii, ask-enter-this-room, ask-put-luggage-here) has no counterpart for item 4; only ashita-shigoto-yasumimasu ('I will take tomorrow off work.') uses the verb.
fix: Add an extras card あしたやすんでもいいですか (ashita yasunde mo ii desu ka, 'May I take tomorrow off?').

claim: The note gives only the doctor's sense of どうしましたか and points to a book page the learner does not have, leaving out the second use the book teaches.
evidence: Book NOTES 2: 'This is a doctor's standard query to a patient ... meaning "what seems to be the problem?" It is also used when asking people in need and means "what is the matter?"' Card note: 'Said by a doctor to a patient (see Notes 2, p. 208).'
fix: Replace the page reference with the book's second use: also said to anyone who looks in trouble, meaning 'What's the matter?'.
